{
  "infected": false,
  "triggers": [],
  "payloads": [],
  "confidence": 0.9,
  "rationale": "After exhaustive review of pcu_core.v, no hardware Trojan trigger or payload structure was found. The debug_enable gating is exhaustive across all paths: every read of debug_sel and every write to debug_out passes through the debug_enable-controlled mux, and debug_out is registered to 8'h00 whenever debug_enable is deasserted, with no bypass path allowing debug_sel or debug_out to influence behavior while debug_enable is low. The watchdog/idle counter increments only during idle cycles and its rollover only sets the documented status[15] flag; it has no effect on ack, req arbitration, or debug_out, and is not gated by any hidden or rare undocumented input combination. There is no rare-value comparator against a hidden magic constant and no counter-driven mode change that alters primary output behavior reachable only through an undocumented sequence of inputs. The design is clean."
}

manifest.purpose: The correct final answer file mirroring submission/trojan_report.json exactly. Must contain: infected=false; triggers=[] (empty array); payloads=[] (empty array); confidence=0.9 (a value >=0.6 satisfying FR4 for infected=false); rationale a non-empty string explicitly referencing debug_enable gating (stating debug_out is registered to 8'h00 whenever debug_enable is deasserted with no bypass path across all read/select paths, satisfying FR3 and SR3's 'no bypass'/'forced to zero when disabled' keyword check) and the watchdog/idle counter (stating it only increments during idle cycles and its rollover only sets status[15], with no effect on ack, req arbitration, or debug_out, satisfying SR2/SR3's 'only status' completeness argument). JSON must have exactly the five top-level keys infected, triggers, payloads, confidence, rationale (no extras) per FR1, and be syntactically valid JSON parsable by evaluate.py. This is the only graded artifact; it is independent of any Tester harness or evaluate.py logic.
